quality.reason: Well-structured digest with specific tickers, attributed sources, engagement metrics for credibility filtering, condensed theses, signal scores, and direct links — genuinely time-saving curation, though it lacks trade parameters (entry/exit/timeframe) and the underlying value still hinges on influencer tweets rather than independent analysis.

Well-structured and scannable with concrete metrics, but contains duplicate signal entries ($ETH alpha_leak listed twice), a malformed empty ticker tag [[]], and truncated news text, indicating dedup and formatting issues that reduce actionable value.

Well-structured review with actionable signal — the BTC alert explicitly flags an assigned strategy underperforming its runner-up by 4.1 points with declining trend, plus capital tracking and per-pair health margins giving clear reassignment decision points.

Specific, actionable whale signals (HYPE orderbook imbalance, 5 whales shorting, full portfolio unwind) presented in a clean scannable format, though identical funding rates across all coins suggests a minor data quality issue.

Well-structured, information-dense review with quantified metrics and clear actionable flags (meta broken 136d, whale-mon 0% uptime, 94.8% signal bridge waste), though minor redundancy between sections and persistently repeated unresolved alerts slightly dilute value.

Well-structured and transparent about its API-failure fallback with verified paper IDs and relevant on-topic papers, but the degraded 3-query web-search methodology likely means incomplete coverage compared to a full arXiv scan, capping its value below a high rating.

The scanner correctly applied skill rules (filtering mechanical expiry-market repricing, honoring SILENT_MODE) and transparently reported a genuine null result, but the output contains no actionable signal—its value is limited to confirming system health and state maintenance rather than delivering insights.

Presents a clear, falsifiable thesis (signal profits driven by SOL beta, not signal accuracy) backed by structured quantitative evidence including a damning negative win-average-move metric, making it directly actionable for deciding whether to retire the signal system.
